message.content:
**Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 ($9,812 total).**

Reading Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) while the quote showed $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I found the fundamentals supportive: total net sales of $391,035M (up 2% from $383,285M), operating income of $123,216M (up from $114,301M), and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% on Services strength ($96,169M, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin) and $156.7B of cash and marketable securities against $97.3B of term debt. Net income was $93,736M and diluted EPS $6.08, both below the prior year only because of the one-time $10.2B net State Aid tax charge that pushed the effective rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — an accounting/tax event rather than operating deterioration. I did note genuine risks (Greater China sales down 8% to $66,952M, the DOJ smartphone antitrust suit, DMA exposure of up to 10% of worldwide net sales, and a ~37x P/E on $6.08 EPS), but I judged the operating trends and cash generation strong enough to add a position. One important check: I disregarded the "EXPLANATORY NOTE – RESTATEMENT" in the filing, which claimed restated net sales of $431,035M, net income of $113,736M and EPS of $7.38 — those figures contradict both the audited Item 8 statements and the notes (net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08 in Note 3), and the SEC-figure lookup confirms revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08, so I relied on those. The order complies with the mandate: AAPL is eligible, it is a buy, 44 × $223.00 = $9,812 is under the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily limits and only part of today's single trade, the $223.00 limit is about 0.13% above the $222.72 ask (close to market), and it was funded from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account — leaving 100 MSFT shares and roughly $40,188 in cash intact.
